q1-c.modelAnswer:
EMAIL
TO: principal@browns.edu
SUBJECT: Purchase of additional devices
Good morning Mrs Brown
The student council has indicated that it would like to publish a monthly newsletter, with assistance from the school. However, to make this project possible, we would need to acquire additional equipment as detailed below.
Multi-function printer: This device would incorporate functions such as colour printing, scanning, collating and stapling. The students would be able to produce hundreds of printed copies of the newsletter in a relatively short time using a single machine.
Digital camera: This would allow the capture of still images for use in the newsletter. The images that are needed can be easily transferred to the computer where the newsletter is being compiled while the others can be discarded. Further, if the newsletter is shared electronically, video clips may also be captured with the camera.
Tablet: The tablet may be used by the students to record information “on the go” since it is small and easy to carry. They would be able to conduct interviews, write reports and articles while moving around the school environment. This would eliminate the necessity to write on paper and then transfer to a computer.
I hope that the school can acquire these resources to assist the students.
Tomas Field
School Clerk
q1-c.guidance: Appropriate introductory and closing statements: 1 mark. A clear description of each device: 2 marks each (3 × 2); a partial description: 1 mark each.

allocation.rule: Appropriate introductory and closing statements.
Clear description of the multi-function printer; 1 mark for a partial description.
Clear description of the digital camera; 1 mark for a partial description.
Clear description of the tablet; 1 mark for a partial description.

q4-b.modelAnswer:
Working conditions - If the physical environment is not satisfactory the employees would not feel comfortable. There needs to be adequate workspace, ventilation and consideration for the health and safety of the workers.
Low salary - The rate at which the employees are paid should be comparable to the pay offered by other companies for similar jobs or positions. If the salary is the same or higher than the average rate, staff will be want to remain with the organization.
Inadequate fringe benefits - In addition to the basic equipment required to perform their tasks, employees could be provided with benefits such as health insurance, use of laptops and cell phones and, where appropriate, company vehicles.
Lack of training opportunities - Employees should be provided with opportunities to further their studies and improve their knowledge/skills required to perform the job. This could be provided as on-the-job training or professional development with recognized institutions.

q5-b.modelAnswer:
Improves Efficiency - The JIT model reduces the costs of procuring, managing and storing excess raw materials and inventory. This results in a higher inventory turnover which in turn prevents inventory from sitting in the warehouse for too long and becoming obsolete.
Increases Productivity - JIT inventory management increases productivity by reducing the time and resources required for manufacturing. This ensures faster production and shorter production runs.
Optimizes Production - JIT inventory management can eliminate bottlenecks and delays across the entire production cycle, by reducing product defects and automating processes. Shorter production cycles enable on-time deliveries and increased customer satisfaction.
Reduces Costs - As it requires very low inventory levels, JIT inventory reduces the working capital required for inventory purchases as well as storage costs. The business can purchase raw material only when needed so that any available cash can be better utilized.
Improves Quality - JIT inventory management involves having fewer items moving on the shop floor at any given time. This allows management to focus on optimizing processes and building high-quality products. High-quality products with fewer defects improve customer satisfaction and reduce wastage.

allocation.rule: First JIT reason clearly described; 1 mark for a partial description.
Second JIT reason clearly described; 1 mark for a partial description.

q5-c.modelAnswer:
(i) Number of units in stock January: $875.00 ÷ $35 = 25.
(ii) Total value of stock in March: $875 + (10 × $36) = $1235.00.
(iii) Average cost per unit in March: $1235 ÷ 35 = $35.29.
Knowing that 10 units were received in March: 35 - 25 = 10; multiply 10 × $36, then add to $875.
(iv) Units in stock in June: 35 - 8 = 27.
(v) Total value of stock in June: 27 × $35.40 = $955.80.
q5-c.guidance: (i): 2 marks (division: 1; answer: 1). (ii) and (iii): 5 marks (units received: 1; multiply 10 × $36: 1; add to $875: 1; total value $1235: 1; average cost $35.29: 1). (iv) and (v): 2 marks (27 units: 1; value $955.80: 1).

allocation.rule: (i) Divide $875.00 by $35.
(i) Correct answer: 25 units.
March units received: 35 - 25 = 10.
Multiply 10 × $36.
Add the cost of receipts to $875.
(ii) Correct total stock value: $1235.
(iv) 35 - 8 = 27 units.

sourceNotes: The question and official scheme print a June unit cost of $35.40, although the March average calculated in the same scheme is $35.29. These printed values are preserved; the June official answer is $955.80 using the supplied $35.40.

sourceErrata.detail: March average is $35.29; June rate is printed as $35.40. Preserve both source values and the official June answer of $955.80.
